topics.label: Introduction to the Lecture
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement system and frames its complexity and significance within immunology.

topics.label: Foundations and Architecture of the Complement System
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overview of complement, explaining its general organization, nomenclature conventions, and the central role of C3.

topics.label: Pathways of Complement Activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways responsible for recognizing pathogens and initiating the complement cascade.

topics.label: Effector Mechanisms of Complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes by which activated complement eliminates pathogens and recruits immune cells.

topics.label: Regulation and Host Cell Protection
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic details the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical Complement Deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic reviews the clinical consequences and disease presentations associated with deficiencies in specific complement components.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Pathogen Evasion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evolve strategies to evade complement-mediated destruction, using Staphylococcus aureus as an example.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer wraps up the lecture and introduces the topic of the upcoming session.
